 Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-15 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Avdija and Damian Lillard took over the third quarter of Tuesday’s 123-103 victory, combining to score 22 of the Trail Blazers’ 38 points. The former supplemented his nine points with three rebounds and three assists in the period, and Deni has scored at least 21 points in eight of Portland’s 10 games. The two teams meet again on Wednesday in what could be another big night for Avdija, who finished Tuesday’s win two assists shy of a double-double. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Deni Avdija tallied 15 points (5-of-13 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 Avdija led the Trail Blazers in points and field-goal attempts on Saturday, but the overall stat line was underwhelming. Deni didn’t shoot well from the field and recorded just one assist. Surprisingly, Avdija’s fantasy value has slipped after Ja Morant’s hamstring injury. Over the last five games, he sits just outside the top-200 in nine-cat formats. Avdija will look to contribute more when Portland hosts Oklahoma City on Tuesday. 
 Deni Avdija 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Deni Avdija recorded 22 points (6-of-12 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), nine rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Lakers. 
 Avdija shot well from the field and finished one rebound shy of a triple-double. However, he also recorded a season-high eight turnovers. In the Trail Blazers’ last four games, Avdija has dished out 30 assists, taking on even more playmaking responsibilities with Ja Morant (hamstring) sidelined. Also, Friday’s eight turnovers were a departure from the norm, as Deni had not committed more than three in any game this season. 
 Deni Avdija 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Deni Avdija led the Trail Blazers with 28 points (10-of-22 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers against the Nuggets on Monday. 
 Avdija stayed hot in this one, and he has now scored at least 20 points in five straight games after being held to 18 points in the season opener. Most of his numbers this season are similar to last year, though his assists are slightly down. The main drop off has been his free throw percentage. After shooting 80.2 percent last year, he’s at 66.7 percent so far this season. If that improves, his overall fantasy value should jump back up.

 Deni Avdija finished Saturday’s win over the Jazz with 24 points (6-of-12 FGs, 10-of-13 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers. 
 Portland’s first game since losing Ja Morant to a hamstring strain went smoothly, as they beat the Jazz by 22. Avdija led the way offensively, shooting a solid percentage from the field. He was one of three Trail Blazers to record multiple assists, along with Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday. Compared to Thursday’s loss to the Grizzlies, Avdija’s usage increased slightly, and it should remain that way until Morant returns. Portland plays four games next week, starting with Denver on Monday.

 Deni Avdija led the Trail Blazers with 24 points (8-of-16 FGs, 8-of-12 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists and one block in a 124-103 loss to the Grizzlies on Thursday. 
 Avdija’s production is slightly down from last season, but he continues to be the primary scoring option for Portland. He only scored 18 points in the season opener, though he only played 24 minutes because of the lopsided score. Since then, he has averaged 24.3 points and 7.3 assists per game while shooting 51.1 percent from the floor. If Avdija can continue to shoot this efficiently, he’ll be even better than he was last season.

 Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Lakers with 23 points (8-of-15 FGs, 3-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists, one steal and four three-pointers. 
 After scoring 11 first-half points on Tuesday, Avdija went quiet in the third quarter, scoring two points on 1-of-4 shooting. But he was front and center when the Trail Blazers needed him most, recording nine points, two rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in the fourth quarter. Thanks in part to Avdija’s stellar play, the Trail Blazers outscored the Lakers 34-26 in the fourth and moved their record to 3-0.

 Deni Avdija got 26 points (8-of-16 FGs, 9-of-12 FTs), six rebounds, six assists, a steal and a three in 39 minutes against the Kings. 
 He had a very prototypical Deni Avdija game. He got you a lot of points, good rebounds, good assists, and a lot of free throw attempts. You would wish he shot better than 75%, but its hard to be too critical after a performance like this. The additions of Ja Morant and Damian Lilliard have not impacted his production that much up to this point which is a relief for owners of Deni in fantasy.

 Deni Avdija amassed 18 points (7-of-16 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Suns. 
 Due to an ankle injury, Avdija was a game-time decision on Wednesday. Cleared to play an hour before tip-off, he started and logged 23 minutes. With the Trail Blazers winning by over 40 points, Avdija didn’t have to extend himself in the season opener. He led the team with 16 shot attempts, a positive development given Damian Lillard and Ja Morant were also in the Blazers’ starting lineup.

 Ajay Mitchell recorded 14 points (6-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and one steal in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Mitchell has scored in double figures in five straight and nine of his last 10 games. Injuries that have beset the Thunder this season have created more opportunities for the third-year guard, who is averaging a career-high 18.5 points per game and providing top-100 fantasy value. As long as Mitchell stays healthy, he’s capable of maintaining his current production all season long.

 Jared McCain tallied 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 After scoring 19 points off the bench in Saturday’s rout of the Wizards, McCain returned to the Thunder starting lineup on Tuesday. Shooting 4-of-7 from beyond the arc, the third-year guard recorded his third 20-point stat line of the season. While he can be inconsistent, McCain is on a bit of a heater, scoring 21, 19 and 21 points in his last three games.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 After playing the entire third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander did not play at all in the fourth, as Portland managed to pull away. Due to Oklahoma City’s many injuries, the two-time MVP is being asked to do even more heavy lifting on offense. SGA’s field-goal percentage suffered on Tuesday, but that doesn’t do much to change his status as one of the most valuable players to roster in fantasy basketball. Oklahoma City plays Portland again on Wednesday, and the extra rest time he picked up in the fourth quarter on Tuesday could pay dividends for SGA.

 Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
 Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori made a change to his starting lineup on Tuesday, replacing Scoot Henderson with Cissoko. While he didn’t shoot well from the field, Sidy finished with a season-high point total and a solid overall stat line in 33 minutes. Henderson played 23 minutes and finished with 11 points, one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers. Cissoko isn’t a must-add, but he’s worth watching, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) out for a few more weeks.

 Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
 Fans got to see “vintage Dame” during the third quarter, with his production helping Portland grab control of the season. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, Lillard scored 13 points in the third. The final three points came on a 35-footer as time expired, giving Portland a 17-point lead heading into the fourth quarter. Lillard didn’t play in the fourth quarter, and the 24 minutes he did play may ensure he’s available for Wednesday’s rematch.

 Achiuwa had to leave Tuesday’s game with just under eight minutes left in the third quarter with a leg contusion and did not return. His early exit gave Dylan Cardwell (1/12/1/2/2) more playing time, and he logged 29 minutes off the bench.  While fellow Kings veteran Domantas Sabonis went scoreless on Tuesday, LaVine had one of his most productive games of the season.
